subject: Private deployment connectivity — choosing the right link for low-latency, audited inference
messages:
From: Sam Green <sam.green@acme-analytics.com>
To: marissa.co@redwood.ai (Marissa Cole)
Cc: netops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity options — quick guidance request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed. We are now scoping the network side for a Redwood Private deployment into our VPCs. Two constraints that matter the most: low tail latency for inference (95p token latency target < 120ms) and strict auditability — all requests must be logged and flow through a small set of managed endpoints for compliance.

Our NetOps asked whether we should pursue VPC peering, PrivateLink, or a site-to-site VPN (we're a multi-region on-prem + cloud shop). They want a recommendation focused on performance, operational overhead, and auditability. Can you summarize pros/cons and a recommended pattern?

Attaching our compliance brief and a rough topology.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Green
Head of Platform Engineering — Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme-llm-privacy-requirements.pdf (PDF)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
To: sam.green@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:02:31 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options — quick guidance request

Hi Sam — thanks for the detail and the attachments. Looping in Karthik (solutions/architecture) and Evelyn (private deployments lead) so we can give a short, pragmatic recommendation and a follow-up checklist for NetOps.

High level preview we will send:
- PrivateLink as primary for strict auditability + minimal attack surface (recommended where supported)
- VPC peering where you need very low network hop count and full-routed access inside cloud VPCs (good for intra-cloud heavy traffic)
- Site-to-site VPN for the on-prem -> cloud leg (encrypted, but higher latency/less predictable throughput than direct/private link)

We can propose a hybrid: PrivateLink fronted endpoints for production inference, VPC peering for data-plane access between VPCs where needed, and a resilient VPN between on-prem and cloud for fallback/offline bursts.

Karthik/Evelyn — can you add specifics on: 1) expected latency delta (approx) between these options, 2) operational tradeoffs (TLS certs, NAT, IP management), and 3) a short runbook for NetOps to validate?

-Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_co@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: sam.green@acme-analytics.com, netops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 11:18:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options — quick guidance request

Sam / Acme NetOps — quick technical summary below (keeps to the three flavors you asked for). I kept numbers conservative and focused on operational impact.

1) VPC peering (cloud-native peering)- Pros:
  - Lowest additional hop count inside the cloud (L3 routing, no NAT by default) — good for intra-cloud traffic between VPCs in same region (expected median add ~1-4ms, 95p depends on AZ separation).
  - No per-connection endpoint management; routing tables handle traffic.
  - Generally lower egress cost inside same cloud region than traffic traversing gateway endpoints.
- Cons: 
  - Not transitive: for multi-VPC topologies you need mesh or transit gateway (adds complexity/cost).
  - Exposes IPs across VPC boundary — larger attack surface if not tightly constrained.
  - Peering across accounts requires IAM coordination and careful route table management.

2) PrivateLink / Interface Endpoints- Pros:
  - Minimal attack surface: traffic goes to an ENI-backed endpoint controlled by Redwood, network path is narrower and easier to audit.
  - Customer keeps source IPs private (we terminate at endpoint), and we can provide per-endpoint logging hooks.
  - Works well for multi-account enterprises where you want controlled ingress with typed endpoints.
- Cons:
  - Slightly higher baseline latency vs peering because of an extra hop to the endpoint and NLB/ENI processing — expect median add ~3-10ms and 95p may be noticeably higher in cold path scenarios.
  - ENI quotas and endpoint scaling need to be considered; depends on throughput (we recommend pre-sizing & autoscale testing).
  - Some cloud features (e.g., cross-subnet hairpin) can complicate fetch patterns; need targeted route table and security group rules.

3) Site-to-Site VPN (IPSec)- Pros:
  - Works for on‑prem connections with encrypted links; good when you need to cross into private datacenter networks.
  - Straightforward to set up with customer gateway and our firewall/VPN appliances.
- Cons:
  - Encryption + encapsulation adds overhead: expect median add ~10-40ms depending on circuits (and more jitter).
  - Throughput ceilings and MTU considerations (path MTU may need lowering on endpoints).
  - Operationally heavier: HA pair configs, rekeying, BGP session management, and NATT traversal issues.

Suggested recommended pattern for your constraints (low tail latency + auditability):
- Production inference endpoints: prefer PrivateLink in each region where you require strict audit and controlled ingress. Use interface endpoints with dedicated NLBs in Redwood VPCs so traffic is funneled to auditable endpoints. This gives the clean compliance boundary and per-endpoint logs.
- For intra-cloud high-throughput internal services (model staging, batch transforms) use VPC peering or a transit gateway to avoid PrivateLink ENI scaling limits and to get the lowest possible latency inside the cloud fabric.
- For on‑prem -> cloud traffic, wire a resilient IPSec S2S VPN for non-latency-critical traffic and a dedicated Direct Connect / ExpressRoute private link if Acme has that option for predictable low latency/high throughput. If Direct Connect is available, prefer it over VPN for production inference traffic.

Operational notes / NetOps runbook (short):
1) Baseline tests: within a pilot VPC, deploy a PrivateLink endpoint + one peered VPC service and measure 95p token latency using your realistic payloads; include TLS handshake time and full request/response. Use iperf for raw throughput baseline.
2) Endpoint sizing: create load tests that simulate 10x expected peak to verify ENI/NLB scaling and surface rate-limiting behavior. Monitor ELB active connections & ENI metrics.
3) Routing & security: lock down security groups to only allow Red-rose (Redwood) endpoint IP ranges; use dedicated route tables for endpoint subnets to avoid accidental routing.
4) Auditing: enable VPC Flow Logs (retention per compliance), ELB access logs, and forward Redwood per-request logs to your SIEM via our forwarding connector.
5) Failover: plan for peering <-> privatelink fallback by using DNS-based routing (weighted records + health checks) or client-side fallback logic.
Evelyn — I left out cert/key lifecycle and HSM guidance; happy to add.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity options — quick guidance request

Sam / Acme team — quick practical checklist and recommendation for your immediate next steps. Keeping this short so NetOps can action.

Our recommendation (practical):
1) Pilot: Stand up a PrivateLink endpoint in your primary region and a peered VPC route to a staging service. Run a 24-hour load window that mirrors production traffic patterns (burstiness & cold-starts). Collect 50k+ samples of latency including TLS handshake.
2) If your 95p stays <120ms with PrivateLink (including TLS) -> roll PrivateLink for production. Implement DNS weight-based cutovers and health checks for gradual rollout.
3) If 95p exceeds target and you have high intra-cloud throughput needs -> use VPC peering/transit gateway for the data plane and keep PrivateLink for control-plane/auditable calls.
4) On-prem: schedule a Direct Connect or ExpressRoute proof-of-concept. If that's not immediately possible, deploy an HA IPSec S2S VPN with BGP and aggressive keepalives, but treat VPN as a fallback for production inference due to jitter.

Checklist items for NetOps (actionable):
- Provide us with VPC/subnet CIDR blocks and ENI quota limits.
- Confirm whether Acme has an existing Direct Connect/ExpressRoute order in process.
- Approve a dedicated subnet for Redwood interface endpoints and an IAM role for endpoint consumption.
- Enable VPC Flow Logs + CloudWatch/Stackdriver export for the pilot period (30d retention preferred).

I'll follow up with a short template network diagram and a pared-down runbook for BGP/policy examples.
Thanks — happy to jump on a 30 minute call to walk NetOps through the pilot checklist.
Evelyn Hart
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
